Hollow SiC/C microspheres were synthesized using a heterogeneous interfacial anti-contraction strategy.
The composition of SiC/C microspheres was controlled by varying the TEOS/resorcinol molar ratio from 0.388 to 0.970.
SiC content in the composites ranged from 27.7% to 39.4%.
The average diameter of the microspheres ranged from 1.27 ± 0.079 to 1.61 ± 0.086 μm.
The thickness of the external shells was about 114 nm for PR@SiO2/PR-3 and increased to about 150 nm for SiO2/C-3.
The density of SiC/C-3 microspheres is 1.7 g cm⁻³.
The average size of SiC nanoparticles is about 5 nm.
The minimum reflection loss achieved was -60.8 dB at 10.4 GHz.
The effective absorption bandwidth reached 5.1 GHz at a thickness of 1.8 mm.
The performance surpasses most previously reported SiC/C composites.
Stability tests showed no significant degradation after exposure to harsh conditions.
RCS simulation confirmed excellent radar stealth performance.
The hollow structure was formed due to preferential carbonization at the interface between the PR core and SiO2 shell.
Carbon shells provide space confinement and slow down silicon species diffusion.
The final composites were treated with HCl to remove MgO impurities.
Higher TEOS dosages preserved the spherical morphology better.
The composites exhibit IV-type N2 adsorption-desorption isotherms.
The specific surface area and pore volume are higher for composites with higher TEOS dosages.
The main dielectric loss mechanisms are conductivity loss and polarization loss.
The composites show good chemical homogeneity and stable morphology after high-temperature processing.
The hollow structure enhances microwave attenuation through multiple reflections.
The material demonstrates excellent environmental tolerance.
The synthesis method is scalable and suitable for practical applications.
The composites have potential applications in stealth technology and electromagnetic protection.
The performance is attributed to the synergistic effect of composition and structure engineering.
